serves_registry_rows: households per leaf (the in-cell weights: how a cell's people divide over tiles of each density class)

sources.name: GHS-POP R2023A, epoch 2020, WGS84, 30 arc-seconds
sources.notice: GHS-POP R2023A, European Commission, Joint Research Centre; Schiavina, Freire, Carioli and MacManus (2023), doi:10.2905/2FF68A52-5B5B-4A22-8F40-C41DA8332CFE; CC BY 4.0.

keys.cell: 1/8 degree; a 30 arc-second pixel goes whole to the cell holding its centre: column floor((lon+180)*8) mod 2880, row floor((90-lat)*8); grid origin as the file states it (-180.0079159 E, 89.0995832 N)
keys.cell_class: 1 village, 2 suburban, 3 terraced, 4 apartment blocks, 5 dense fabric: lower bounds 0, 250, 1500, 6000, 12000 people per km2 of the cell's whole area; cells under 1 per km2 are not read (twin/globe a29e87d)
keys.tile_class: 0 empty (under 1 per km2 of the tile's own area), then the five

envelope.regions: world, not split by region (the twin's region table is not yet published as data)
envelope.classes: all five cell classes; the smallest holds 121 cells
envelope.grain: about 0.9, 1.9 and 3.7 km; nothing below about 1 km is resolved

law: each of the four share vectors in a row sums to 1,000,000 within 300 parts (the 'each cell once' means were accumulated in single precision; a consumer should renormalise); the table is consumed as weights for an exact apportionment, whose output obeys the section law
checker: python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('transition_table.json'));assert all(abs(sum(r[k])-10**6)<=300 for r in d['rows'] for k in ('tiles_each_cell_once','people_each_cell_once','tiles_by_people','people_by_people'))"  and, on the consumer's apportioned output, cargo run -p holon-scene --example check_sums -- <file.jsonl>

verdict.reason: this is a reading of the reference, not a certificate: no generator has been scored against it, and it carries no budget and no consumer. A generator that uses these weights is unscored until its own tiles are compared with the grid.

limits: a lower bound on unevenness: the file is a resampling of the publisher's equal-area grid and nothing below about 1 km is seen
the fine grid is itself a model (census counts spread over built-up area)
coastal cells read as uneven because sea pixels hold nobody and the cell class uses whole area
holds_no_real_feature: This table holds no coordinate, id, name or tag of any real feature. It holds 15 rows of counts and shares by class.
edge_columns: pixel column 0 holds 18.81 people and lands in cell column 2879; pixel column 43201 holds 0.00 and lands in cell column 0. The file's two extra columns do not double-count.
